title: Decide the doctor exit-code contract
description:
evalctl's `doctor` exits 0 even when a component is unhealthy. Sibling tool
spoolctl exits 3 in the same situation and reports readiness as `data.ready`.
evalctl's behavior is pinned by a test, so it is deliberate, but the two tools
in the same family disagree on what a health check's exit code means -- and
callers that script both will get it wrong for one of them.

This is not blocked by the failure_reason adoption work or by the conformance
sweep, and neither changes it. It needs its own decision.
acceptance_criteria:
- A decision is recorded: evalctl either keeps exit 0 with an unhealthy
  component, or adopts a nonzero exit, with the reasoning stated.
- If the behavior changes, the pinning test and any documented exit-code table
  are updated together.
- The decision states whether `data.ready` is adopted as the machine-readable
  readiness signal.

title: Canceled spoolctl job is misdiagnosed as an incompatible spoolctl
description:
A spoolctl job canceled before it runs reports `state: canceled`,
`attempts: []`, `last_failure_reason: null`. Against that payload,
`latest_terminal_attempt` (`evalctl/runner.py:257`) raises
`E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE` with the message "spoolctl show did not include
attempts" -- blaming tool compatibility for an ordinary queue outcome.

Not reachable through evalctl's own flow today: evalctl never cancels, and it
drains synchronously. Reachable by an external `spoolctl cancel` against the
run's `.spoolctl.db`.

Reproduction: queue a job, run `spoolctl cancel` against it before the worker
picks it up, then `spoolctl show --json` -- the job carries an empty `attempts`
list. Verified against real spoolctl 0.4.11.

Deliberately not fixed alongside the failure_reason adoption work: the
resolution likely needs a decision on the `canceled` case status, which exists
in `TERMINAL_CASE_STATUSES` (`evalctl/run_state.py:16`) with nothing producing
it. Giving it a producer is a contract decision, not a passenger on an
unrelated batch.
acceptance_criteria:
A canceled job with no attempts must not be reported as spoolctl
incompatibility.
close_reason: Fixed in 33c6521. latest_terminal_attempt returned E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE for a job canceled before a worker ran it, because such a job reports an empty attempts list and that was not distinguished from a missing attempts key. It now returns None for a present-but-empty list; the queued loop synthesizes a spawn_failed result (runner_result_for_unrun_job), which normalizes to E_RUNNER_FAILED on that case while the run completes. A missing or non-list attempts key still raises E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE. Deliberately does not give the 'canceled' case status a producer -- that stays a separate contract decision. Coverage: FAKE_SPOOLCTL_DROP_ATTEMPTS knob for the end-to-end run, direct unit tests over latest_terminal_attempt and runner_result_for_unrun_job, and a real-spoolctl test that queues a job, cancels it pre-execution, and feeds the real show payload through latest_terminal_attempt. The end-to-end test was verified to fail against the pre-fix read with the exact envelope reported here.

title: Implement runner execution contract
description: The runner is the agent-under-test invocation, and v0.1 must execute it honestly as arbitrary local code while bounding reproducibility and artifact leakage.
design:
Support `runner.argv` with `shell:false` as the default and `runner.command` with `shell:true` as an explicit escape hatch. Exactly one form is valid for the selected mode. Default `cwd` to the per-case workspace. Inherit only `env_allowlist` variables and always inject `EVALCTL_CASE_FILE`, `EVALCTL_WORKSPACE`, `EVALCTL_OUTPUT_FILE`, `EVALCTL_TASK_FILE`, and `EVALCTL_DIFF_FILE` when present.

Close stdin by default, with `runner.stdin:"task"` to pipe task text. Apply `timeout_seconds`, kill the process group on timeout, capture stdout/stderr/output up to `max_output_bytes`, and apply `redact_env_values` and `redact_patterns` before writing artifacts.
acceptance_criteria:
- `shell:false` executes argv without implicit shell joining; `$EVALCTL_*` substitution is performed only by evalctl.
- `shell:true` executes the explicit command through `sh -c` and is documented as the less-safe escape hatch.
- Runner spawn failures and timeouts mark the case `error`; ordinary nonzero process exits are captured and scored rather than treated as tool errors.
- Every `run` emits `W_UNSANDBOXED_RUNNER` in the JSON envelope and prints the warning to stderr when appropriate unless the suite explicitly acknowledges it.
- Captured stdout, stderr, and output are truncated and redacted before persistence, with booleans recording whether truncation or redaction occurred.

title: Capture workspace manifests
description: The core differentiator is scoring the resulting workspace, so evalctl must capture structured before/after filesystem evidence rather than relying on textual diffs.
design: Walk the per-case workspace before and after runner execution to produce `workspace-before.json` and `workspace-after.json`. Derive `workspace-diff.json` from those manifests. Include untracked and ignored files. Represent files, directories, symlinks, and other special file types. Use POSIX-style relative UTF-8 paths with no `.` or `..` segments and no absolute paths.
acceptance_criteria:
- Full manifests contain entries with `path`, `kind`, and file hashes where applicable.
- Directories are represented by presence; binary files are represented by sha256; symlinks are not followed and store target information.
- Unreadable or unsupported non-UTF-8 paths emit `W_PATH_UNREADABLE` and do not silently corrupt the manifest.
- `workspace-diff.json` identifies added, modified, and deleted paths from the two structured manifests.
- Textual `workspace.diff` is best-effort and never parsed by scorers.

title: Implement deterministic built-in scorers
description: v0.1 must grade runs with deterministic local scorers that are credible without an LLM judge and can be recomputed from persisted artifacts.
design: Implement built-in scorers for `exact`, `contains`, `regex`, `json-schema`, `numeric-threshold`, `file-exists`, `exit-code`, and `workspace-diff`. Each scorer emits `{ok, score, label, findings}` and respects whether it is required or advisory. Built-in scorers consume persisted, redacted outputs and structured workspace manifests.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each scorer has unit tests for pass, fail, and malformed-input behavior.
- `workspace-diff` matches `expect.files_changed` and `expect.files_forbidden` using glob semantics against `changed_paths[].path`.
- `exit-code` compares expected exit code against `runner.json` and does not conflate failed expectations with tool errors.
- Required scorer failures produce case status `fail`; scorer crashes or invalid scorer inputs produce case status `error`.
- Score output is stable and can be serialized into each case `score.json`.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic built-in scorers for text, regex, exact, JSON parse, numeric threshold, file existence, exit code, and workspace diff — commit 449ded0

title: Implement synchronous run orchestration
description: v0.1 needs one complete synchronous execution path that can run a suite, invoke runners, score cases, and continue through partial failures without depending on async infrastructure.
design:
Implement `evalctl run <suite> [--jobs N] [--timeout S] [--run-id <id>] [--fail-on-fail] [--json]`. Create a reservation for the run id, materialize a fresh workspace per case, execute cases with bounded concurrency, write artifacts, derive scores, update `manifest.json` atomically, and continue after case-level errors with `W_PARTIAL_RUN`.

Default `--jobs` to `min(CPU_count, 4)`. Sort iteration before serialization so JSON is deterministic regardless of completion order. Use `<UTC-timestamp>-<suite-name>` for default run ids. Reusing a completed matching run id returns the existing run; live reservations return `E_RUN_BUSY`; semantic clashes return `E_RUN_CONFLICT`.
acceptance_criteria:
- `run` produces a complete run directory under `evals/runs/` with a suite snapshot and per-case artifacts.
- Case errors do not abort the whole run; the run remains reportable and emits `W_PARTIAL_RUN`.
- Eval failures exit 0 by default and set `data.run.ok:false`; `--fail-on-fail` exits 6 when any case is not `pass`.
- A live reservation returns exit 4 with `E_RUN_BUSY` and a retry recommendation; a completed mismatched run id returns exit 5 with `E_RUN_CONFLICT`.
- JSON output includes paste-ready follow-up commands only for implemented verbs.
close_reason: Implemented synchronous run orchestration with per-case workspaces, run directories, scoring, partial-run warnings, run-id reuse, and fail-on-fail exit behavior — commit 449ded0

title: Build portable run directory model
description: The run directory is the v0.1 source of truth, so it must carry everything needed to inspect, report, and re-score a completed run without relying on shell history or the original suite location.
design: Write `manifest.json`, `suite-snapshot/`, and per-case `input.json`, `task.txt`, `runner.json`, stdout/stderr captures, `output.*`, before/after workspace manifests, derived `workspace-diff.json`, best-effort `workspace.diff`, and `score.json`. Keep every path recorded inside the run directory relative to the run-directory root. Treat `report.md` as a convenience copy; regenerate authoritative reports from manifest and artifacts.
acceptance_criteria:
- No artifact path inside `manifest.json`, score files, or report payloads is absolute.
- `suite-snapshot/` is sufficient for `status` and `report` to interpret scorer configuration from a copied run directory.
- `created_ts` and run ids are treated as volatile metadata and excluded from canonical report hashes.
- `score.json` is persisted for inspection but is not trusted as input during artifact replay.
- The run directory layout is documented by `robot-docs guide`.
close_reason: Implemented portable run directory layout with manifest, suite snapshot, per-case artifacts, relative manifest paths, and replay-safe score recomputation — commit 449ded0

title: Implement status and report commands
description: Agents need diagnose and triage commands that summarize run state, rank failures deterministically, and point to the exact artifacts needed for inspection.
design:
Implement `status <run-id|--run-dir <path>> [--json]` and `report <run-id|--run-dir <path>> [--format markdown|json] [--json]`. Resolve run ids under `evals/runs/`; accept copied standalone run directories through `--run-dir`. Rank report failures as `error` before `fail`, then by ascending aggregate numeric score, then case id.

`status` should include per-case state and a `recommended_action`. `report` should include aggregate scores, ranked failures, relative artifact links, and `data.report_hash` over the normalized report projection.
acceptance_criteria:
- `status` works for both local run ids and copied run directories.
- `report --format json` and `report --json` both return the universal envelope.
- Markdown reports are deterministic apart from explicitly volatile metadata.
- Ranked failures are ordered by error/fail class, aggregate score, and case id.
- `commands[]` contains only implemented follow-up commands such as regenerating a JSON report.
close_reason: Implemented status and report commands for run ids and copied run directories with ranked failures, report_hash, markdown, and JSON envelopes — commit 449ded0

title: Add real-spoolctl CI coverage
description:
Queued-run semantics are verified in CI only against a fake spoolctl fixture.
That fixture is built from evalctl's own expectations, so by construction it
cannot notice when the real tool's contract moves — which is how a contract bump
broke every queued run and stayed undetected across nine spoolctl releases.

A compatibility fix whose only evidence is the fixture that missed the
incompatibility is not proven. Real-binary coverage closes the blind spot that
produced the outage.

Do not release v0.4.2 until this epic is merged and passing in CI. This is a
release blocker, not merely a dependent task: dependency order makes it next,
but only an explicit stop makes it required.
acceptance_criteria:
- Queued-run semantics are exercised against a real pinned spoolctl in CI.
- The job cannot pass by skipping its tests.
- Local test discovery is unaffected when spoolctl is not installed.
- v0.4.2 is not released until this epic is merged and passing.

title: Add real-spoolctl integration test module
description:
No test drives evalctl's queued path against a real spoolctl binary. Every
queued behavior evalctl depends on — outcome mapping, artifact reconstruction,
report determinism — is currently verified only against a fixture that agrees
with evalctl by construction.
design:
Add a test module driving the installed spoolctl binary. Coverage:

    queued vs in-process report-hash parity
    queue provenance in the run manifest
    nonzero runner exit scored, not reported as an infrastructure error
    runner timeout mapped to E_RUNNER_TIMEOUT
    spawn failure mapped to E_RUNNER_FAILED
    the stdin:"task" runner wrapper
    resume after an interrupted queued run

Nonzero-exit scoring earns its place: conflating a failing task with broken
infrastructure would silently corrupt eval results rather than error loudly.

The module skips when spoolctl is absent so local discovery is unaffected. An
environment variable, set only in CI, converts a missing or below-floor binary
into a hard failure at import.

Keep any test-helper sharing to the minimum this module needs. A general
refactor of the existing CLI test helpers is separate work and must not ride
along here.
acceptance_criteria:
- All listed behaviors are exercised against the real binary and pass.
- The module skips cleanly when spoolctl is absent.
- With the CI environment variable set and spoolctl missing or below the floor,
  the module fails with a message naming the required version.
- No unrelated refactor of existing test modules is included.
close_reason: Added tests/test_real_spoolctl.py (commit 5e62569), 10 tests driving the installed spoolctl binary rather than the fake fixture. Covers all seven behaviors from the design plus three that fell out of it: the advertised floor is satisfiable by a published release, and capabilities and doctor both report the observed version and contract. Skip/hard-fail contract works in all four combinations, each verified by hand: spoolctl absent and EVALCTL_REQUIRE_REAL_SPOOLCTL unset skips 10; absent with the variable set raises at import naming the cause and the fix; a below-floor 0.4.4 binary with the variable set raises naming the observed version and the floor; below-floor without the variable skips. The version and contract under test are printed to stderr at import so a CI log records what it proved. Full discovery: 96 tests OK with real spoolctl 0.4.11 on PATH and the variable set (2 skips, both pre-existing and unrelated), 96 OK with spoolctl absent (12 skips). Ran the new module three times for flakiness; stable. No shared test-helper refactor: the CLI helpers are a small local harness, and the reason is recorded in a comment at the class so a later reader does not read the duplication as an oversight. One design correction found while writing: the resume test's reference run must be taken after the slow runner fixtures are installed, or the hash comparison fails on a fixture difference rather than on the interruption. The test also asserts a case was genuinely left unfinished, so it cannot pass on a run that had already completed.

title: Add queue-integration CI job with hard guard
description:
Real-binary tests that no CI job runs provide no protection. The job must also
be unable to report success while silently skipping the tests it exists to run —
a self-skipping job would reproduce the original blind spot in a form that looks
green.
design:
Add a `queue-integration` job to the CI workflow: checkout, set up Python,
install pinned `spoolctl==0.4.11`, print the spoolctl version and contract under
test for the log record, then run the real-spoolctl test module with the
require-real-spoolctl environment variable set.

The pin uses `spoolctl==0.4.11` as the reproducible input and deliberately adds
no separate hash pin in this release; PyPI publishes only that release and one
alpha, so the version pin is unambiguous. Recording the decision here prevents a
future reviewer treating the absent checksum as an oversight.

Failure rule:

    Local: spoolctl absent            -> skip
    CI:    spoolctl absent or too old -> hard failure
acceptance_criteria:
- A `queue-integration` job exists and runs the real-spoolctl tests.
- The job installs `spoolctl==0.4.11` and logs the version and contract tested.
- The require-real-spoolctl variable is set in the job environment.
- Removing spoolctl from the job makes it fail rather than skip.
- The workflow file parses and the existing test job is unchanged.
close_reason: Added the queue-integration job to .github/workflows/ci.yml (commit 121dac1). Steps: checkout, setup-python 3.11, pip install 'spoolctl==0.4.11', 'spoolctl capabilities --json' as the log record of the version and contract under test, then 'python -m unittest tests.test_real_spoolctl -v' with EVALCTL_REQUIRE_REAL_SPOOLCTL=1. The variable is what makes the job unfalsifiable: a missing or below-floor binary fails at import instead of skipping to a green result. Chose Python 3.11, the oldest supported runtime, and confirmed spoolctl 0.4.11 declares Requires-Python >=3.10 so the pin installs there. Dropped a 'spoolctl --version || true' logging line in favour of the capabilities envelope alone - it carries both tool_version and contract_version, so no step needs a failure-swallowing fudge. The absent hash pin is documented inline as a decision. The existing test job is unchanged; git diff shows the workflow change is purely additive. Verified locally by running the job's exact test command with the variable set and spoolctl on PATH (10 tests OK) and by parsing the workflow as YAML to confirm both jobs and all step names resolve.

title: Adopt spoolctl failure_reason in queued runs
description:
Queued-run classification in `runner_result_from_spoolctl_attempt`
(`evalctl/runner.py:264`) infers *why* an attempt ended from two proxies that
evalctl does not own:

    timed_out = state == "timed_out" and exit_code is None
    spawn_failed = exit_code is None and (state in {"failed", "abandoned", "canceled"}
                                          or str(attempt.get("error") or "").startswith("spawn failed:"))

Both exist because spoolctl 0.4.1 had no machine-readable failure enum. It has
had one since 0.4.2, and since evalctl v0.4.2 the floor guarantees it: contract
>= 2 is required, every spoolctl at that contract advertises `failure_reasons`
in `capabilities` and emits `attempts[].failure_reason`, and the probe enforces
this on every queued run.

Two defects:

- Fragility. A prefix match on a human error string is a contract spoolctl can
  reword in any release. Nothing would fail loudly; evalctl would silently
  reclassify a spawn failure as a clean exit. The state-set proxy has the same
  shape.
- A live bug. `runner.py:280` reads `attempt.get("duration_ms")`, a field real
  spoolctl never emits, so **every queued case records `duration_ms: 0`**.
  Observed on the scaffolded suite: queued `cr-fail`/`cr-pass` both `0`;
  the same suite in-process, `14` and `15`.

Why the tests did not catch the duration bug, which is the part worth
remembering: the fake fixture emits `duration_ms` (`tests/fakes.py:125`)
because it was written against evalctl's expectations rather than spoolctl's
output. The real-spoolctl job would only catch it if something asserted on
duration, and nothing does. Report-hash parity did not catch it and
structurally cannot -- `duration_ms` lives only in `cases/<id>/runner.json`,
appearing in neither `case_manifest_entry` (`evalctl/scoring.py`) nor the
report projection (`evalctl/reports.py`). The queued run reproduced the exact
v0.4.2 report hash while carrying wrong durations in every case. Hash parity
proves the scored projection agrees; it says nothing about artifact fidelity
outside it.

Scoped honestly: this is mostly a robustness deletion. For every outcome
evalctl can reach today, old and new classification agree -- `spawn_failed`
and `worker_crash` land where the old state-set landed, `timeout` matches,
`process_exit` with a concrete exit code matches. The value is one owned
contract instead of two borrowed proxies, less code, and the `duration_ms`
fix, which is the only real behavior change. Do not write a changelog entry
implying queued runs were misclassifying outcomes; nothing observed shows that.

This epic is the whole of release v0.4.3.
design:
Evidence gathered against real spoolctl 0.4.11 (`.venv/bin/spoolctl` inside
the project checkout; it is not on PATH), by driving four jobs to terminal
states:

| job | attempt `state` | `exit_code` | `failure_reason` | job `state` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `echo hi` | succeeded | 0 | null | done |
| `exit 7` | failed | 7 | process_exit | dead |
| `sleep 5`, timeout 1 | timed_out | null | timeout | dead |
| `/nonexistent/binary` | failed | null | spawn_failed | dead |

A *successful* attempt carries `failure_reason: null`, not `process_exit`.
`process_exit` means the process ran and its exit code is the fact, pass or
fail. Job state for failures is `dead`, never `failed`.

`capabilities --json` advertises `failure_reasons: [process_exit, timeout,
spawn_failed, worker_crash, canceled, unknown]`.

Full real attempt key set: `attempt_no, error, exit_code, failure_reason,
finished_at, started_at, state, stderr_path, stdout_path, worker_id,
worker_pid`. `started_at`/`finished_at` are epoch-second floats.

Base for implementation: current `main` head (`e91d73b`, `v0.4.2-3`), which
carries the trusted-publishing workflow, the `.DS_Store` ignore and the PyPI
install note on top of the `v0.4.2` tag. Branch from the head, not the tag.
No release branch wanted.

Binding decisions:

- Classification keys on the pair `(failure_reason, exit_code)`. Attempt
  `state` is never consulted. Two sources for one fact is how they drift, and
  `state` is the source being retired. `failure_reason` says why it ended;
  `exit_code` supplies the process fact `process_exit` refers to.
- An unrecognized `failure_reason` maps to the `unknown` behavior and is not an
  error. A sibling tool adding an enum member must not take evalctl down. No
  `E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE`, no maximum-known-enum constant to go stale.
- `worker_crash` and `canceled` map to `E_RUNNER_FAILED`, not to a new state.
  Infrastructure failure with no process-exit fact is exactly what
  `E_RUNNER_FAILED` already means here.
- Accept newer spoolctl, do not gate on it. No raise of the required version.

Non-goals for the whole epic: no change to evalctl's `contract_version` (stays
1), envelope shape, error codes, exit codes, or report projection; no new case
status (`canceled` stays a producer-less member of `TERMINAL_CASE_STATUSES` in
`run_state.py:16` -- giving it a producer is its own contract decision); no
change to the spoolctl floor, the probe, or `doctor`; no test-helper
extraction.
acceptance_criteria:
- Queued classification reads `attempts[].failure_reason` and `exit_code`, and
  never the attempt's `state`.
- No string match on runner error text remains in `evalctl/runner.py`.
- A queued case's `duration_ms` matches its real duration, asserted against the
  real binary with fixed bounds.
- An unrecognized `failure_reason` yields `E_RUNNER_FAILED`, never
  `E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE`.
- The fake's attempt payload matches real spoolctl field-for-field for every
  field evalctl reads.
- `pyproject.toml` and `evalctl/__init__.py` both report `0.4.3`.
- Negative: report hashes unchanged. Capture the scaffolded `code-review`
  suite's report hash before any change and assert it is byte-identical after;
  it must still begin `sha256:89f6dee9` and end `bac88e`.
- Negative: no new case status, error code, or exit code.
- Negative: the existing real-spoolctl timeout and spawn-failure tests pass
  unedited. If either needs editing, the change is larger than this epic
  claims -- stop and re-plan rather than editing the test.
- Full suite green both with and without spoolctl installed;
  `queue-integration` green on a remote.

title: Correct the fake spoolctl attempt payload to the real field set
description:
The fake spoolctl in `tests/fakes.py` synthesizes an attempt record written
from evalctl's expectations rather than from spoolctl's real output. It emits
`duration_ms` (`tests/fakes.py:125`), a field real spoolctl 0.4.11 never
emits, and omits `failure_reason`, which real spoolctl always emits. That
divergence is what hid the live `duration_ms: 0` bug from the entire suite --
the same blind-spot class as the earlier contract-version outage.

Separately, four `failure_reason` values -- `worker_crash`, `canceled`,
`unknown`, and any future member -- cannot be produced by the real binary in
CI. The fake must be able to synthesize them, which is precisely the
synthetic-failure role the fake was narrowed to.
design:
Real attempt key set to match: `attempt_no, error, exit_code, failure_reason,
finished_at, started_at, state, stderr_path, stdout_path, worker_id,
worker_pid`. `started_at`/`finished_at` are epoch-second floats.

Reason values follow the real binary: `None` on success, `process_exit` on
nonzero exit, `timeout`, `spawn_failed`.

Control surface, named now so it cannot grow ad hoc. Two environment variables
read by the fake's `work` path, following the existing `FAKE_SPOOLCTL_TRANSIENT`
precedent (`tests/fakes.py:80`):

    FAKE_SPOOLCTL_FAILURE_REASON=<string>   override the synthesized failure_reason
    FAKE_SPOOLCTL_EXIT_CODE=<int|empty>     override the synthesized exit_code
                                            (empty string means null)

Environment variables rather than `install_fake_spoolctl` kwargs, because one
installed fake must vary per invocation within a single test, and because
`work` is spawned by evalctl and inherits the test process environment.

Binding constraint: these override **only the synthesized attempt record**.
They must not change whether or how the real subprocess runs. If they do, the
fake stops being a fake of spoolctl and becomes a fake of the test's
expectations -- the exact failure this work exists to undo.

Sequencing note: dropping `duration_ms` from the fake breaks the current
`runner.py:280` read until the duration task lands. Commit the two together if
the tree must stay green at every commit.
acceptance_criteria:
- The fake's attempt record carries `failure_reason`, `started_at` and
  `finished_at`, and no longer carries `duration_ms`.
- The payload matches real spoolctl 0.4.11 field-for-field for every field
  evalctl reads.
- Synthesized reasons match the real binary: `None` on success, `process_exit`
  on nonzero exit, `timeout` on timeout, `spawn_failed` on spawn failure.
- `FAKE_SPOOLCTL_FAILURE_REASON` overrides the synthesized reason, including
  with a value that is not a known enum member.
- `FAKE_SPOOLCTL_EXIT_CODE` overrides the synthesized exit code; an empty
  string yields a null `exit_code`.
- Neither variable changes whether or how the subprocess runs -- demonstrated
  by a test that sets a knob and still observes the real command's stdout.
close_reason: Fake spoolctl now synthesizes the real 0.4.11 attempt key set (attempt_no, error, exit_code, failure_reason, finished_at, started_at, state, stderr_path, stdout_path, worker_id, worker_pid); duration_ms is gone. Reasons match the real binary: null on success, process_exit, timeout, spawn_failed. FAKE_SPOOLCTL_FAILURE_REASON and FAKE_SPOOLCTL_EXIT_CODE override only the synthesized record, applied after the subprocess runs; a test sets each knob and still reads the real command's stdout. Fake and real binary are both asserted against the shared REAL_SPOOLCTL_ATTEMPT_KEYS constant, so drift on either side fails. Also made the fake's stream paths absolute, matching real spoolctl. Commit 139c4e9.

title: Key queued classification on failure_reason and exit_code
description:
`runner_result_from_spoolctl_attempt` (`evalctl/runner.py:264`) decides
`timed_out` and `spawn_failed` from the attempt's `state` field and from a
prefix match on `attempt["error"]` against the literal `spawn failed:`. Both
are contracts evalctl does not own: spoolctl can reword the error string or
change its state vocabulary in any release, and evalctl would not fail loudly
-- it would silently reclassify a spawn failure as a clean exit.

spoolctl has emitted a machine-readable `attempts[].failure_reason` since
0.4.2, and evalctl's v0.4.2 floor (contract >= 2) guarantees it is present on
every queued run. The proxies have no remaining justification.
design:
Replace the two proxies with a lookup keyed on the pair
`(failure_reason, exit_code)`. No row consults attempt `state`.

| `failure_reason` | `exit_code` | `timed_out` | `spawn_failed` | resulting `error_code` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| null / absent | 0 | False | False | none -- score normally |
| null / absent | nonzero or absent | False | True | E_RUNNER_FAILED |
| process_exit | concrete | False | False | none -- score normally |
| process_exit | absent (malformed) | False | True | E_RUNNER_FAILED |
| timeout | any | True | False | E_RUNNER_TIMEOUT |
| spawn_failed | any | False | True | E_RUNNER_FAILED |
| worker_crash | any | False | True | E_RUNNER_FAILED |

The last row is the forward-compatibility rule: an unrecognized reason is

must not take evalctl down.

title: Compute queued duration_ms from attempt timestamps
description:

and **every queued case records `duration_ms: 0`**.

    queued  (--queue spoolctl):  cr-fail duration_ms=0    cr-pass duration_ms=0

title: Assert real queued duration against the real spoolctl binary
description:

binary, which is the single missing assertion that would have caught every

failure message as a diagnostic, never as a pass condition.

title: Fix spoolctl capability probe
description: Evalctl advertises optional queued execution through spoolctl, but the probe path currently assumes a simplified capabilities shape that differs from real spoolctl output. Evalctl currently unwraps only the data payload and attempts to build a set directly from those flag objects, causing an internal TypeError before queued execution can start. This undermines the optional queue integration even though standalone evalctl execution remains useful.
design:
Keep the fix local to evalctl's spoolctl probing and test fixtures. Preserve the existing queue runner semantics for add, work, wait, show, and outcome mapping. Do not change spoolctl's capabilities contract or raise evalctl's minimum supported spoolctl version above 0.4.1.

The implementation should make real spoolctl envelope metadata available to the probe, normalize supported add flags from either string entries or structured objects, and distinguish soft capability discovery failures from hard queued-run failures.

- Evalctl capabilities reports real compatible spoolctl as available when spoolctl is on PATH.
- Evalctl queued runs can pass the probe and execute through compatible real or real-shaped spoolctl.
- Incompatible or malformed spoolctl probe responses never surface as Python tracebacks, TypeError, or generic internal errors.
- Capabilities discovery failures remain soft degradation: evalctl capabilities exits successfully with spoolctl unavailable.
- Queued run and queued resume probe failures remain hard evalctl envelope errors.
- No changes are required in spoolctl.

title: Normalize spoolctl probe parsing
description: The spoolctl capabilities probe currently reads version fields only from unwrapped data and assumes add flags are plain strings. Real spoolctl uses top-level envelope tool_version and structured flag objects, so evalctl must normalize the real shape while retaining compatibility with the older compact string-flag shape.

Update probe_spoolctl() to call the envelope-preserving helper from the previous task. Use the existing envelope discriminator: isinstance(payload, dict) and "ok" in payload. For envelope payloads, require ok:true and object data. Decide explicitly whether non-envelope raw object capabilities output should remain supported; if it remains supported, add a test for that path, otherwise reject it as E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE.

Extract the version from envelope-level tool_version first, then data-level tool_version, then data-level version. Treat envelope-level tool_version as authoritative when present, including when reporting integration version through capabilities_data(). Extract contract_version from capabilities data.

Add a small normalizer such as spoolctl_flag_names(flags) that accepts a list of strings or a list of objects with string "flag" fields and returns a set of flag names. - Missing or malformed version fields reject cleanly without an internal error.
- The returned probe data includes a normalized version value usable by capabilities_data().

title: Fix spoolctl contract-version floor
description:
`evalctl run <suite> --queue spoolctl` fails with `E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE`
(exit 3) against every spoolctl release that can currently be installed. The
entire queued execution path is unusable.

The compatibility probe in `evalctl/spoolctl.py` requires spoolctl's
`contract_version` to equal `"1"` exactly. spoolctl bumped `CONTRACT_VERSION`
to `2` in its 0.4.5 release, so every release from 0.4.5 onward is rejected.
Verified by running both binaries together: patching only that equality check
makes the full queued path work end to end, so the gate is the sole blocker.

An equality pin on a sibling tool's contract turns each of that tool's routine
releases into an evalctl outage. The same failure recurs at contract 3 unless

title: Add integration contracts module with spoolctl floors
description:
The supported spoolctl version is hard-coded as the literal `0.4.1` in at least
five places: the compatibility gate, three error hints, the `capabilities`
integrations block, and the robot-docs prose. Scattered literals are the
mechanism by which the advertised minimum went stale while the gate said
something different.

A single home for integration policy prevents the next drift.
design:
Add `evalctl/integration_contracts.py` holding `MINIMUM_SPOOLCTL_VERSION`
("0.4.11"), `MINIMUM_SPOOLCTL_CONTRACT` (2), and one shared upgrade hint string.

Deliberately a new module rather than `static_contract.py`: that module is
evalctl's own machine-contract surface, and mixing runtime integration policy
into it means a future hint-string tweak drags the static contract and its
golden files along. Both `spoolctl.py` and `static_contract.py` import from the
new module, which also avoids a circular import (`spoolctl.py` already imports
`static_contract`).

Stdlib only. This work adds no runtime dependency.
acceptance_criteria:
- `evalctl/integration_contracts.py` exists with the two floor constants and one
  shared hint string.
- No `0.4.1` literal remains in `evalctl/` as a spoolctl minimum.
- Both `spoolctl.py` and `static_contract.py` source the values from the new
  module.
- No import cycle; full suite still passes.

title: Parse spoolctl contract version numerically
description:
The probe reads spoolctl's contract version as a string. Replacing the broken
equality check with a string comparison such as `contract >= "2"` would sort
`"10"` before `"2"` and recreate the same forward-compatibility failure one
spoolctl release later — the exact bug class this work exists to remove.

The comparison must be numeric.
design:
Add a parser converting the observed contract to `int`. Accept integer `2` and
string `"2"` — spoolctl's JSON type for this field is not guaranteed. Reject
missing, empty, non-numeric, and non-positive values as
`E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE` (exit 3, unchanged).

Malformed values raise with the same `observed_contract` and `minimum_contract`
fields as the below-floor case, so consumers see one error shape per cause
rather than one shape for old-but-valid values and another for garbage.
acceptance_criteria:
- Integer `2` and string `"2"` both parse and are accepted.
- Contract `"10"` is accepted, proving the compare is numeric not lexicographic.
- Missing, empty, non-numeric, and non-positive contracts raise
  `E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE`, never a traceback.
- Every rejection carries `observed_contract` and `minimum_contract`.
close_reason: Added parse_spoolctl_contract() in evalctl/spoolctl.py. Accepts int 2 and str "2"; contract 10 and 17 parse above 2, proving the compare is numeric not lexicographic. Missing, empty, non-numeric, non-positive, bool, and non-scalar values raise E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE (exit 3) with observed_contract and minimum_contract, never a traceback; error dicts asserted JSON-serializable. Two unit tests added. Parser is deliberately not wired into the gate here - that is evalctl-npw.4. Suite 78 tests, OK, 2 skipped. Commit 06f48f9.

title: Reject prerelease spoolctl versions below the floor
description:
The existing `version_tuple` helper takes the numeric prefix of each
dot-segment and discards the rest. Verified behavior: `0.4.11-rc1`,
`0.4.11rc1`, `0.4.11.dev1`, and `0.4.11+local` all map to `(0, 4, 11)`, so a
release candidate of the floor release passes as though it were the final
release.

That is the same class of sloppiness as the contract equality check — a version
comparison that quietly does the wrong thing. Leaving it implicit inside the
work that fixes that class is not defensible, so the policy is chosen and
pinned rather than inherited by accident.
design:
Policy:

    Accept final versions >= 0.4.11.
    Reject prerelease-like versions whose base version is not above 0.4.11.
    Accept local/build metadata when the base final version is >= 0.4.11.

So `0.4.11rc1` is rejected (base equals the floor, and an rc precedes its
final); `0.4.12rc1` and `0.5.0a1` are accepted (base above the floor);
`0.4.11+local` is accepted.

Small local parser with its own tests. No `packaging` dependency — evalctl is
stdlib-only and this work does not change that.

Keep the parser small on purpose. The version floor is a proxy; the contract
floor and the `add`-flag check are the substantive capability gates, and a
prerelease genuinely missing a capability is caught by those regardless.
acceptance_criteria:
- `0.4.11rc1` is rejected.
- `0.4.12rc1`, `0.5.0a1`, and `0.4.11+local` are accepted.
- `0.4.11` is accepted; `0.4.9` is rejected.
- No new runtime dependency is introduced.

No new runtime dependency - local parser, stdlib only. Wired into the compatibility gate and the pinned prefix-policy CLI test flipped to assert rejection. Suite 80 tests, OK, 2 skipped. Commit deec095.

title: Split spoolctl compatibility gate into three checks
description:
One boolean expression currently decides three unrelated questions — is the
version new enough, is the contract the right one, are the required `add` flags
present — and raises a single message, "spoolctl is missing required evalctl
queue capabilities", for all of them. A user whose spoolctl is merely a
contract version ahead is told flags are missing.

The contract half of that expression is also the outage: it tests equality
where it must test a floor.
design:
Replace the single expression with three checks, each raising
`E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE` (error code and exit code 3 both unchanged, so this
is not a contract change) and each carrying its own machine-readable fields:

    version below floor / prerelease of floor -> observed_version, minimum_version
    contract below floor / missing / malformed -> observed_contract, minimum_contract
    missing add flags                          -> missing_flags (sorted list)

The contract check compares `>=` against the floor constant, never equality.
A comment must record why, naming this incident: the equality form looks more
careful and will otherwise be "corrected" back by a future reader.

Newer-than-floor contracts are accepted with no upper bound. There is
deliberately no maximum-tested constant, and therefore no newer-contract
warning and no degraded state — without such a constant "newer than tested"
cannot be computed, and a constant that must be bumped on every spoolctl
release will go stale.
acceptance_criteria:
- Three distinct failure messages, one per cause, each with its fields.
- Contract 2 accepted; contracts 10 and 17 accepted.
- Contract 1 rejected with observed and minimum contract reported.
- Version below the floor rejected with observed and minimum version reported.
- A missing required `add` flag is rejected and named in `missing_flags`.
- `E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE` and exit 3 are unchanged.
close_reason: probe_spoolctl() now runs three separate checks, each raising E_SPOOLCTL_INCOMPATIBLE (exit 3, unchanged) with its own fields: version -> observed_version/minimum_version, contract -> observed_contract/minimum_contract, flags -> missing_flags (sorted). Contract compares >= MINIMUM_SPOOLCTL_CONTRACT, never equality, with a comment naming this incident so a future reader does not 'correct' it back. No maximum-tested constant, so no upper bound and no newer-contract warning. Test asserts three distinct messages and their fields; contract 1 rejected, version below floor rejected, missing --max-crashes named. Landed with evalctl-npw.5 in one commit because raising the contract floor alone fails every fake-fixture queued-run test. Suite 81 tests, OK, 2 skipped. Commit 6cd5cf0.

default represents the supported world, and the overrides are the deviations
under test.

- Existing queued-run tests pass without per-test version overrides.

title: Add forward-compatibility regressions for newer contracts
description:
The defect being fixed is a forward-compatibility bug: evalctl rejected a
spoolctl contract newer than the one it was written against. A test suite that
only pins today's contract value would reproduce the same outage one spoolctl
release from now and call it passing.

The regression that matters is not "contract 2 works" but "a contract we have
never seen works".
design:
Drive the probe with contracts 2, 10, and 17 and assert all are accepted.
Contract 10 does double duty: it also proves the comparison is numeric rather
than lexicographic, since `"10" < "2"` as strings.

Add a comment recording why the test exists, so a future reader does not
simplify it back to a single current-value assertion.
acceptance_criteria:
- Contracts 2, 10, and 17 are all accepted by the probe.
- A test comment records the forward-compatibility rationale.
- Tests fail if the gate is reverted to an equality check.

title: Report spoolctl contract version in capabilities
description:
The `capabilities` integrations block reports only a spoolctl version and a
minimum version. Version alone cannot diagnose a contract mismatch, which is
precisely the failure this work fixes — a user reporting "queued runs are
broken" gives no way to see which contract their spoolctl speaks or which one
evalctl wants.
design:
When spoolctl is available, the integrations block reports:

    {"available": true, "planned": false, "minimum_version": "0.4.11",
     "minimum_contract": 2, "version": "0.4.11", "contract_version": 2}

When spoolctl is unavailable or incompatible, behavior stays soft — exit 0,
`available: false` — and the block keeps `minimum_version` and
`minimum_contract`, so a user can see what was required without a working
spoolctl.

Contract fields are integers, consistent with numeric parsing.
acceptance_criteria:
- `minimum_version` and `minimum_contract` are always present.
- Observed `version` and `contract_version` are present when spoolctl is
  available.
- Contract fields are integers.
- Absent spoolctl still exits 0 with `available: false`.
close_reason: Capabilities integrations.spoolctl always carries minimum_version and minimum_contract; when spoolctl is available it also carries observed version and contract_version. Contract fields are ints, asserted by isinstance. Absent spoolctl still exits 0 with available:false and both minimums present. Capabilities golden re-pinned: diff is the added minimum_contract field plus the data_hash. Suite 83 tests, OK, 2 skipped. Commit a3e0ae8.

title: Fix doctor spoolctl recommendation and pin exit code
description:
`evalctl doctor` correctly detects an unusable spoolctl and reports the
component as `unhealthy`, then recommends running
`evalctl doctor --component spoolctl --fast --json` — that is, running the
diagnosis again. Diagnosing correctly and prescribing a re-run of the diagnosis
is a doctor-quality defect independent of the version gate. The absent-binary
path also recommends installing a version that was never published.

Separately, `evalctl doctor` exits 0 even with a component in `unhealthy`
state. That is a live behavior question worth deciding deliberately later, so
this work pins the current behavior rather than changing it in passing.
design:
The incompatible branch recommends an install command naming the floor version,
with the probe's own message as rationale, plus the alternative of running
without `--queue spoolctl`. The absent-binary branch names the same installable
version. Neither may recommend running `evalctl doctor`.

Report the observed contract version in the component's `observed` block.

Exit codes are explicitly unchanged. Add a test asserting an unhealthy spoolctl
component still exits 0, so that a future decision to change doctor's exit
contract is made deliberately rather than discovered as a regression.
acceptance_criteria:
- Incompatible spoolctl yields a recommendation to install or upgrade, with the
  run-without-queue alternative.
- Absent spoolctl recommends an installable version.
- No doctor recommendation invokes `evalctl doctor`.
- Observed contract version appears in the component's observed block.
- A test pins that an unhealthy component still exits 0.

Observed contract_version and minimum_contract appear in the component's observed block on both healthy and incompatible paths. title: Bound jobs list pagination

title: Fake spoolctl show returns a flat job dict; real one nests it under job
description:
The fake spoolctl fixture's `show` verb emits the job record flat, with `state` and `attempts` at the top level. Real spoolctl 0.4.11 emits {job: {...}, attempts: [...], events: [...]}, where the job's own state lives at job.state and only attempts/events are top-level.

evalctl/runner.py writes per-case job.json as {job_id, state: detail.get("state") or attempt.get("state")}. Against the real binary detail.get("state") is always None, so the first branch is dead and job.json records the ATTEMPT state ("succeeded") rather than the JOB state ("done"). Against the fake the first branch wins and records the fake's flat state. Two different provenance values, and the fixture hides which one ships.

This is the same class of defect as the duration_ms bug fixed under evalctl-ede: the fake was written from evalctl's expectations rather than from spoolctl's output, so a read that never works against the real tool looks covered. The attempt key set is now asserted against both sides by REAL_SPOOLCTL_ATTEMPT_KEYS; the enclosing show envelope is not.
design:
Two parts, in order.

1. Make the fake's show envelope match real spoolctl: {job: <flat job dict>, attempts: [...], events: []}. Extend the two-sided drift check that REAL_SPOOLCTL_ATTEMPT_KEYS already performs for attempt keys so it also covers the show envelope's top-level key set. A future divergence in the wrapper then fails a test instead of being absorbed.

2. Decide and pin what job.json's `state` means. The two candidates are the job's terminal state (done, failed, canceled) and the last attempt's state (succeeded, failed, timed_out). The job state is the better provenance record -- it is what an operator sees from spoolctl -- but changing it is visible in run artifacts.

Constraint carried from evalctl-ede: tests/test_real_spoolctl.py's test_queued_run_records_queue_provenance_in_the_manifest passes today because the real path records "succeeded". Whichever value is chosen, that test must be updated deliberately as part of this issue, and the choice stated in the changelog rather than silently reconciled.
acceptance_criteria:
- The fake's show payload has the same top-level key set as real spoolctl's, asserted from one shared constant against both the fake and the real binary.
- job.json's `state` records the same value whether a run goes through the fake or the real binary, and a test asserts that.
- The chosen meaning of job.json `state` is documented, and the changelog names the change if the recorded value moves.
- The full suite passes with and without spoolctl on PATH.

title: Add command-scorer protocol
description:
`run_scorer` is a closed dispatch over eight deterministic built-in scorers; there is no
way to score a case with an external program. v0.2 adds a `command` scorer type — the
external scorer seam that is also the future LLM-judge seam — so a suite can score a case
by running an arbitrary program that emits a JSON verdict. Because report and replay
recompute case status from artifacts and never trust `score.json`, a non-deterministic
external scorer must be captured as an artifact, not re-executed.
design:
Add a `command` branch to `run_scorer`, and thread `case_dir: Path` and `execute: bool`
through `score_case` and `run_scorer`. `run_case` calls with `execute=True`;
`recompute_case_score` calls with `execute=False`.

Scorer config entry:
`{"name":"command","id":"<unique>","required":bool,"argv":[...]|"command":"...","shell":bool,"timeout_seconds":N}`.
The `id` is required for command scorers (a suite may have several, all named
`"command"`), must be path-safe (no separators, no `..`, no unsafe filename chars), and
names the verdict artifact.

Execute path (run time): invoke once per case with `EVALCTL_CASE_FILE` (persisted
`input.json`), `EVALCTL_OUTPUT_FILE` (persisted `output.txt`), and `EVALCTL_WORKSPACE`;
cwd is the case workspace; argv/command gets the same `$EVALCTL_*` substitution as the
runner. Persist the parsed verdict to `cases/<case_id>/scorers/<id>.json`. This artifact
is a runner-class input, captured once, never regenerated.

Replay path (report time): read the persisted verdict artifact; never execute. Deterministic
scorers keep recomputing as today.

Process hardening (mirror the runner): `subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True)`
with `os.killpg` process-group kill on timeout; `timeout_seconds` from a named default
when omitted; byte-capped stdout/stderr with decode-and-replace; apply the suite's
redaction patterns and redacted env values before persisting; write capped/redacted
`cases/<case_id>/scorers/<id>.stdout.txt` and `.stderr.txt` for debugging.

Verdict normalization: stdout must parse as exactly one JSON object after trimming
whitespace (extra non-whitespace output is a scorer error); `ok` required boolean;
`score` required finite numeric constrained to 0.0..1.0 (reject NaN/Infinity and
out-of-range); `label` required string, normalized to `"pass"`/`"fail"` from `ok` when
missing/empty; `findings` required list, string entries normalized to `{"why": <string>}`.
`error:true` from a zero-exit process is a case error.

Status mapping: required scorer `ok:false,error:false` -> case `fail`; advisory scorer
`ok:false` does not fail the case; `error:true` or any normalization failure -> case
`error` regardless of `required`. A nonzero exit, timeout, or unparseable/invalid verdict
produces a scorer result carrying `error:true` and `error_code:"E_SCORER_CASE_FAILED"`,
which drives the case to `status:"error"` via the existing `s.get("error")` path — never
an orchestrator abort.

Carry the scorer `id` through every scores projection: the result object, the manifest
case entry, and the report/status failure projections — omitting the key when absent so
deterministic-only suites' `report_hash` is byte-unchanged.

Add `E_SCORER_CASE_FAILED` to the code registry (class `tool-env`, surface `score_json`
as a machine-token parallel to `runner_json`, where `["run","replay"]`); keep the
existing envelope-abort `E_SCORER_FAILED` distinct. A command-scorer is arbitrary local
code covered by the existing always-in-envelope unsandboxed-runner warning.
acceptance_criteria:
- A suite with a passing command-scorer scores the case pass and writes `cases/<id>/scorers/<id>.json`.
- Copy the run dir, delete the scorer binary, and `report --run-dir <copy>` reproduces the original `report_hash` (verdict is an artifact, never re-executed).
- Two command scorers, one passing and one failing: the report identifies the failing scorer by `id`.
- Invalid `score` type, NaN/Infinity, missing `ok`, extra stdout, and `error:true` from a zero-exit process each yield case `error`; a required scorer `ok:false,error:false` yields `fail`; an advisory scorer `ok:false` does not fail the case.
- A nonzero-exit or non-JSON scorer yields `status:"error"`, `W_PARTIAL_RUN`, run exits 0 (6 under `--fail-on-fail`), no envelope `errors[]`.
- Command-scorer timeout kills the process group; stdout/stderr are byte-capped and redacted in the persisted debug artifacts.

- Added verdict normalization, per-case scorer failure handling, scorer id projection, timeout process-group kill, redacted/capped debug artifacts.
- Added CLI-surface tests for command-scorer pass/fail/error/advisory/timeout behavior.

title: Implement replay --failed execution replay
description:
Only artifact replay exists today: a copied run dir reproduces its report, but there is
no way to re-execute a failed case after fixing the runner or fixtures. `replay --failed`
re-runs only the failed/errored cases of a prior run against the current suite, into a
fresh run linked to the source, so a fix turns a red case green in a new run. `manifest.replayed_from`
is already reserved but never populated.
design:
Add `evalctl replay --failed <source-run-id|--run-dir PATH> [--suite S] [--run-id NEW] [--force] [--json]`
with its own source parser — do NOT reuse `resolve_run`, which strips only
`--run-dir`/`--format` and would misread `--failed`/`--run-id`. Exactly one source is
required (positional id XOR `--run-dir`; both or neither -> `E_CASE_INVALID`). `--run-id`
is destination-only. `--failed` is the only selector in v0.2; missing it -> `E_CASE_INVALID`.

Select failed targets from `report_data(source_run)` (the recomputed projection), NOT
from stored `manifest.cases[].status` — the manifest status is a run-time summary, while
the authoritative reportable state is recomputed from artifacts (command-scorer verdicts
included). Targets are cases whose recomputed `status != "pass"`. Use the manifest only
for provenance and id/artifact metadata.

Resolve the current suite: default to `manifest.suite.name` resolved the way `run`
resolves a suite; `--suite <suite-or-path>` overrides (needed because the manifest stores
only suite name+hash, `suite.json.name` can differ from the directory, and a copied
`--run-dir` may sit where `evals/suites/<name>` does not exist). Resolution failure ->
`E_SUITE_NOT_FOUND` with a hint to pass `--suite`. Intersect targets with the current
suite's cases; a selected case absent from the current suite is dropped with
`W_REPLAY_CASE_ABSENT`, never fabricated.

Produce a coherent PARTIAL run over exactly the re-executed cases: fresh run dir (default
run id `<source>-replay-<UTC-ts>`, `--run-id` overrides), snapshot the CURRENT suite,
re-run the selected cases through the shared executor. Factor the executor loop out of
`command_run` into a shared `execute_cases(...)` helper both call. Write the manifest with
`replayed_from = <source run_id>` and `cases[]` = the replayed subset; `manifest.suite.case_count`
is the subset count, explicitly not the full current suite count. Emit the always-in-envelope
unsandboxed-runner warning (replay re-executes runner code) and `W_PARTIAL_RUN` when any
replayed case errors.

Overwrite gating: fresh dir needs no gate. `--run-id` naming an existing completed run
requires `--force`; without it -> `E_RUN_CONFLICT` (exit 5). `--force` does not remove a
busy reservation dir (stays `E_RUN_BUSY`). Reject destination == source even under
`--force` (e.g. `--run-id r1` on source `r1`, or a `--run-dir` destination resolving to
the source path) with `E_RUN_CONFLICT` before writing anything, so replay never destroys
the source it needs.

Zero targets (all-green source) is a successful no-op: exit 0 with
`{"replayed_from":...,"cases_replayed":0}` and `W_NOTHING_TO_REPLAY`.

Add `W_REPLAY_CASE_ABSENT` and `W_NOTHING_TO_REPLAY` to the registry; add `replay` to the
`where` of `E_RUN_CONFLICT` and the unsandboxed-runner warning.
acceptance_criteria:
- A red case + a runner fix, then `replay --failed <run>`, yields a fresh run whose `manifest.replayed_from` is the source id, containing only the previously-red case, now `status:"pass"`, exit 0.
- Deleting/corrupting the source `cases/*/score.json` still lets `report <source>` name the red case AND `replay --failed` select the same case (selection from `report_data`, not the manifest summary).
- An all-green source yields `cases_replayed:0`, `W_NOTHING_TO_REPLAY`, exit 0.
- Source id both before and after replay flags resolves to the same source; `--run-dir PATH --run-id NEW` keeps source and destination distinct; missing `--failed` -> `E_CASE_INVALID`; both positional source and `--run-dir` -> `E_CASE_INVALID`.
- A suite whose `suite.json.name` differs from its directory, run by path, then replayed with `--suite <path>` after a fix, resolves and re-runs correctly.
- `--run-id` onto an existing completed run without `--force` -> `E_RUN_CONFLICT` exit 5; with `--force` overwrite succeeds; `replay --failed r1 --run-id r1 --force` -> `E_RUN_CONFLICT` exit 5 with the source manifest byte-identical.
- A selected case removed from the current suite -> `W_REPLAY_CASE_ABSENT`, skipped.
notes:
COMPLETED:
- Added replay --failed with a dedicated source parser, --suite override, projection-based failed selection, partial run manifests, zero-target no-op behavior, overwrite/source guards, and absent-case warnings.
- Factored the run executor into execute_cases shared by run and replay.
- Added CLI-surface tests for replay grammar, current-suite fixes, projection selection, overwrite guards, --suite override, and absent cases.

title: Add suite add authoring verb
description:
Suites can only be created by `init_project`, which scaffolds the fixed sample. There is
no way to create a new empty suite from the CLI, forcing hand-authored JSON. `suite add`
creates a minimal valid suite that `case add` and `scorer add` then fill.
design:
Add `evalctl suite add <name> [--runner-argv "..."] [--runner-command "..."] [--shell] [--json]`.
Create `evals/suites/<name>/` with a minimal valid `suite.json` (name,
`cases: "cases.jsonl"`, a runner block from the flags with the v0.1 defaults for
`timeout_seconds`, `max_output_bytes`, `env_allowlist`, empty redaction), an empty
`cases.jsonl`, and a `fixtures/` dir. Runner form is mutually exclusive (`--runner-argv`
XOR `--runner-command`+`--shell`), validated up front the way `validate_suite` validates
runner config.

The `<name>` is path-contained: reject path separators, `..`, empty segments, or any name
that normalizes outside `evals/suites` with `E_CASE_INVALID`.

Atomic multi-file creation: a new suite is a directory plus multiple files, so per-file
atomic writes do not prevent a half-created suite dir. If the destination already exists,
decide idempotent-match vs conflict before writing anything. Otherwise build a temporary
sibling dir under `evals/suites/`, populate it fully, run `validate_suite` on it, then
`os.replace`/rename into place only on success.

Idempotency: an existing suite dir with a byte-identical `suite.json` -> `created:false`,
return name. Existing with different content -> `E_RUN_CONFLICT` (exit 5). Never overwrite
an authored suite. An empty suite (zero cases) validates as `case_count:0, valid:true`.
acceptance_criteria:
- `suite add demo --runner-argv "python3 $EVALCTL_WORKSPACE/r.py"` creates `evals/suites/demo/{suite.json,cases.jsonl,fixtures/}`, and `validate demo` passes with `case_count:0`.
- Re-running the identical command -> `created:false`.
- The same name with a different runner -> `E_RUN_CONFLICT`, exit 5.

title: Add case add authoring verb
description:

valid case to an existing suite, assigning and returning its id, so a suite can be built

design:
Add `evalctl case add <suite> --task "..." --workspace <path> [--id ID] [--diff <path>] [--expect-json '<json>'] [--json]`.
Append one line to `cases.jsonl` in the existing on-disk form (one `stable_json(case)`
per line, trailing newline) so unrelated cases do not churn.

Canonical construction order (this is how idempotency is judged): parse flags -> build the
body WITHOUT id -> compute the generated id if `--id` is absent (the same rule
`load_cases` uses: content-hash slice) -> set `id` -> serialize with `stable_json`. Retry
comparison is against that canonical body including the generated id, so a retry never
looks different merely because one object had an explicit id and the other did not.

`--expect-json` parses into the case's `expect` field, not a new `expect_json` field; an
absent/empty `--expect-json` omits `expect` entirely (does not write `"expect": {}`) and
retries must match that choice.

`..` with `E_CASE_INVALID`; store normalized POSIX-relative paths. The workspace (and diff
if given) must also exist under the suite dir, matching the validator.

Same id, different canonical body -> `E_RUN_CONFLICT` (exit 5). Reuse the existing
duplicate-id guard. Run `validate_suite` after the write; on failure roll back the
appended line by restoring the prior file bytes.

design: Add conforming handlers for capabilities, schema, robot-docs guide, help, and version. Normalize namespace dispatch for `suite add`, `case add`, and `scorer add` through one small helper. Keep `run --resume` behind `command_run()` or wrap it so the public handler shape remains consistent.
acceptance_criteria:
- `evalctl --help`, `capabilities`, `schema`, and `robot-docs guide` outputs remain stable against normalized goldens.
- `evalctl --version` remains covered by version-shape and package-metadata assertions.
- Unknown namespace subcommands still return `E_UNKNOWN_SUBCOMMAND`.
- Normalized wrappers delegate to existing behavior without changing the public command contract.

title: Re-run the make-cli conformance sweep after v0.4.3
description:
No fix lands inside the conformance sweep. This bead produces findings only.
A defect found here becomes its own bead with its own acceptance criteria.

The standing positioning guardrail: a passed conformance gate expires when the
surface it covered changes. Since the last review the surface changed three
times -- v0.4 added `doctor`, `plan`, bounded `jobs list` and `did-you-mean`;
the CLI extraction broke `cli.py` into fourteen modules; v0.4.2 changed the
spoolctl integration's error surface. The failure_reason adoption work changes
queued runner artifacts again, which is why this sweep runs after it.

The deliverable is a findings document plus beads. Any fix it justifies is
scoped, prioritized and released separately. The failure mode to avoid is the
sweep quietly becoming a refactor.

Method is binding: **verify by running the CLI.** The rule exists because the
v0.1 section-16 checklist recorded a bounded `jobs list` as met when it was
not. Reading the source is how the last checklist was wrong.
design:
Archetype: make-cli build/task-orchestrator (`references/archetypes.md`
sketch 5), which weights PLAN and DIAGNOSE heaviest. Calibrate every weight to
that sketch.

Checklists: the per-verb and before-ship lists in make-cli `SKILL.md`.
Pre-flight is re-derived once for the tool as a whole, not per verb.

The fifteen shipped verbs, from `capabilities`: `capabilities`, `case`,
`doctor`, `init`, `jobs`, `plan`, `replay`, `report`, `robot-docs`, `run`,
`schema`, `scorer`, `status`, `suite`, `validate`.

Sweep order is heaviest archetype weight first, so a sweep cut short has still
covered what matters: `plan`, `doctor`, `run`, `jobs`, `status`, `report`,
`replay`; then the authoring verbs `suite`, `case`, `scorer`, `init`; then
introspection `capabilities`, `schema`, `robot-docs`, `validate`.

Beads are created from the findings list *after* the document is written, so
prioritization happens over the whole picture rather than verb by verb.
acceptance_criteria:
- All fifteen verbs are covered by the per-verb checklist, none skipped.
- Every "met" row carries a pasted invocation **and** cites the reference file
  it was judged against; no row is marked met from source reading or from
  memory of a principle.
- The pre-read reference set is read before the first row is marked.
- The before-ship checklist is re-run in full, determinism check included.
- Each seed observation is confirmed or refuted by an invocation.
- The findings document exists and is committed alongside the roadmap.
- Findings become beads with acceptance criteria; no fix lands inside the
  sweep itself.
- The roadmap records the sweep's date and outcome, so the next expiry is
  measurable against it.

title: Read the make-cli reference set and re-derive pre-flight
description:
No fix lands inside the conformance sweep. This bead produces findings only.
A defect found here becomes its own bead with its own acceptance criteria.

make-cli's `SKILL.md` is a spine that defers the actual contract text to
`references/`, loaded on demand. Naming only the two checklists would let the
sweep mark rows from memory of what a principle says -- the same class of
error as marking them from source reading. Both are banned.

The binding rule for the whole sweep: **a checklist row may be marked only
from two things together -- the applicable reference text, and a pasted
invocation with its output.** This task establishes the first half of that
pair before any row is marked.
design:
Read before the sweep starts, for the tool as a whole:

    references/archetypes.md      calibrate every weight to sketch 5
    references/envelope.md        the universal envelope and meta
    references/introspection.md   capabilities, schema, robot-docs, --help
    references/errors.md          error text, corrected command, safe alternative
    references/determinism.md     the X; X; diff gate
    references/mega-commands.md   PLAN and DIAGNOSE shape (weightiest here)
    references/async.md           jobs, reservations, --wait
    references/safety.md          destructive paths, --yes/--force gating

Read on demand, when a verb raises the question and before that row is marked:
`streaming.md`, `config.md`, `composability.md`, `conventions.md`,
`schema-evolution.md`.

Pre-flight is re-derived once here for the tool as a whole, not per verb.
acceptance_criteria:
- All eight pre-read reference files have been read, before any checklist row
  is marked.
- The pre-flight checklist is re-derived once for the tool, with the result
  recorded for the findings document.
- The findings document's method section states the two-part marking rule
  (reference text plus pasted invocation).

title: Confirm or refute the four conformance seed observations
description:
No fix lands inside the conformance sweep. This bead produces findings only.
A defect found here becomes its own bead with its own acceptance criteria.

Four observations were gathered while planning the sweep. **They are leads,
not findings.** Each must be re-verified in its own right by invocation, and
the sweep must not stop at them.

One of these leads was itself wrong on first pass, which is the reason the
rule exists: a probe looked for a top-level `mega_commands` key, found none,
and concluded evalctl advertised no mega-command mapping at all. False. The
lesson carried forward: an absent top-level key is not evidence about per-verb
data. Check the level the contract actually specifies.
design:
Lead 1 -- mega-command metadata is per-verb, with no top-level index.
Verified: `capabilities --json` reports
`data.verbs.doctor.mega_command == "DIAGNOSE"` and
`data.verbs.plan.mega_command == "PLAN"`, set in
`evalctl/static_contract.py:131` and `:146`, copied out by
`capabilities_entry_from_spec`, and already asserted in
`tests/test_evalctl.py`. The open question is narrower:

    capabilities advertises mega-command roles per verb, but not as a top-level
    mega-command index. The sweep must decide whether per-verb metadata is enough.

`references/mega-commands.md` decides it. Related and genuinely absent:
sibling spoolctl, same archetype, additionally publishes `probe_vocabularies`,
`totality`, `contract_policy`, `code_registry`, `job_states` and
`attempt_states` at the top level; evalctl publishes none of those. Whether
any is required is for the sweep to decide.

Lead 2 -- the inferctl doctor probe looks already compliant.
`probe_inferctl_component` (`evalctl/doctor.py:135`) reports
`route_available`. The standing question of whether v0.4's route capture got
doctor coverage looks like a confirm, not a gap. Say so explicitly and close
the question rather than carrying it a third time.

Lead 3 -- bounded-list coverage beyond `jobs list`. v0.4 bounded `jobs list`
only. Any other verb returning an unbounded collection owes the same
`--limit`, cursor and truncation message.

Lead 4 -- `tool_version` is pinned literally at `tests/test_evalctl.py:226`,
so a version bump edits a test. Known and deliberate; decide whether it stays
deliberate.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each of the four leads is confirmed or refuted by a pasted invocation, not
  by source reading.
- Lead 1 produces an explicit decision on whether per-verb mega-command
  metadata suffices, judged against `references/mega-commands.md`, plus a
  decision on each of the six top-level keys spoolctl publishes and evalctl
  does not.
- Lead 2 is closed explicitly, either as a confirm or as a gap -- it is not
  carried forward a third time.
- Lead 3 names every verb returning an unbounded collection.
- Lead 4 records a decision.
- No code fix is made in this bead.

title: Create beads from the conformance findings and record the sweep
description:
No fix lands inside the conformance sweep. This bead produces findings only.
A defect found here becomes its own bead with its own acceptance criteria.

A findings document with no tracker entries decays into a document nobody
implements from. Beads are created here, after the whole picture exists, so
prioritization spans all fifteen verbs rather than happening verb by verb.

The pressure this ordering resists is real and predictable: most conformance
findings will be two-line fixes, and fixing one while it is in front of you is
faster than writing it up. That is precisely how an audit turns into an
unreviewed refactor, and how the resulting record stops describing any surface
that ever existed.

The roadmap also needs the sweep's date and outcome recorded, because the
standing guardrail -- a passed conformance gate expires when the surface it
covered changes -- is only measurable against a recorded date.
design:
For each finding, create a bead with its own acceptance criteria, priority set
from the archetype weight recorded in the findings document. Fixes are scoped
and released separately from the sweep; none of them lands in this epic.

Then edit the roadmap to record the sweep's completion date and outcome.

- Every finding in the document has a corresponding bead with its own
  acceptance criteria.

- The roadmap records the sweep's date and outcome.
- The epic can be closed: no finding is left tracked only in the document.

title: Fix Fake Spoolctl Fixture Races
description:
Roadmap section 4.1. CI run 30072965277 failed on the Python 3.13 matrix job in test_queue_spoolctl_outcome_mapping_and_stdin_wrapper with a JSONDecodeError. Root cause is the fake spoolctl fixture, not any real spoolctl integration path.

In evalctl/tests/fakes.py the generated fake binary does an unguarded read-modify-write against a single shared .spoolctl.db: save() (fakes.py:46) is a plain write_text, load() (fakes.py:41) re-reads the whole file. Under --jobs, evalctl invokes the fake once per case concurrently, exposing three races:

1. Torn read - a reader observes a partially written file. This is the observed JSONDecodeError. Fixed by atomic rename.
2. Lost update - two add processes both load, both mutate, both save; the second clobbers the first job entry. NOT fixed by atomic rename.
3. Colliding job ids - job_id = "job-" + str(len(data["jobs"]) + 1) (fakes.py:82) derives the id from a snapshot both processes read before either wrote, so two cases can receive the same job-N. NOT fixed by atomic rename.

An atomic write alone is insufficient. Races 2 and 3 need a lock held across the entire read-modify-write (O_EXCL lockfile or fcntl.flock), with the atomic rename on top. Shipping only the atomic write leaves the fixture flaking intermittently rather than reliably, which is worse for a fixture because it reads as a real regression.

Acceptance:
- Fake .spoolctl.db writes use a same-directory temp file plus os.replace.
- The full load-mutate-save sequence in the fake add and work paths is serialized under a lock so concurrent fake processes cannot lose an update.
- Job-id assignment is unique under concurrency and not derived from a possibly-stale len(data["jobs"]).
- The fix does not expand the fake fixture ownership of real queue semantics. It stays a contract-shape and synthetic-failure fixture; real queue semantics coverage is roadmap 4.2.
- The Python 3.13 failing test path is covered locally or in CI.
- Ordinary local unit-test discovery still passes with no real spoolctl installed.

Out of scope: pinned real-spoolctl CI coverage (roadmap 4.2), spoolctl 0.4.2 failure_reason adoption.
close_reason: Atomic .spoolctl.db writes plus flock and counter-based job ids; regression test added
